title: A rate-of-progress panel ranks the reactions that matter at one condition, and a species trace shows when they take over
summary: The 3 by 3 grid ranks the eight largest net reaction rates at nine conditions, each panel scaled to its own maximum. The species trace shows one ignition in time: slow growth of intermediates, then a step. Together they show which steps drive the chemistry and when.

media.alt: A three by three grid of horizontal bar charts titled top-8 rate-of-progress spectra by condition, normalized per panel. Each panel lists eight hydrogen-oxygen reactions with bars from minus one to plus one, blue for net forward and red for net reverse, and its title gives temperature, pressure, equivalence ratio and the peak absolute rate in mol per cubic metre per second. The peak rates range from about 1e-13 to 7e5.

source.caption: Rate-of-production spectra
source.note: Group explainer. The ROP grid is titled rate-of-progress (per reaction), while the page text calls it rate-of-production (per species); the species trace's title says mole fraction but its y axis reads Y, and the numbers match mass fractions (computed).
group: 07_09_rop_spectra: Rate-of-production spectra, 3 by 3 grid across nine conditions (representative)
08_04_species_profile_case-50: Species profile, case 50: mass fractions against time at phi 6, 1000 K, 100 atm

read_the_figure.question: Which reactions carry the chemistry at each condition, and how do the species evolve through ignition?
read_the_figure.axes: ROP grid: each panel has the eight reactions with the largest net rates of progress on the y axis (names as written); x is the net rate divided by the largest absolute rate in that panel, from -1 to +1; blue bars are net forward, red net reverse. Panel titles give T, P, phi and the peak |ROP| in mol/(m^3 s). Species trace: x time in ms (0 to 2); left y the major species Y (0 to 0.09), right y the radicals (dashed) Y from 0 to 0.005; title gives H2/O2/N2 = 0.461538 : 0.0384615 : 0.5, phi = 6, T = 1000 K, P = 100 atm.
look_at: Read the top bar of each ROP panel: the leading reaction. At 1000 K and 100 atm it is H2 + OH <=> H + H2O; at 1900 K it is H2 + O <=> H + OH; in the 2800 K, 0.1 atm, phi 0.3 panel the leader is a reverse (red) reaction, HO2 + OH <=> H2O + O2.

Compare panel titles for the peak |ROP|: from 7.18e5 mol/(m^3 s) at 2800 K, 100 atm, phi 0.3 down to 1.84e-13 at 2800 K, 0.1 atm, phi 6. Every bar is scaled to 1 in its own panel, so these panels look equally busy and are not.
Species trace: before about 1.6 ms the major species change slowly while H2O2 (purple dashed) grows steadily to about 0.005; then at about 1.64 ms everything changes at once.
After ignition the right-hand radicals are zero on this scale, H2O sits at about 0.086, and H2 at about 0.048.
read_the_figure.proves: Which reaction dominates under which condition, and that ignition is an abrupt event preceded by a slow build-up of a pool of intermediates. It says nothing about whether the numbers are right without data.
if_wrong: Per-panel normalisation hides absolute size: a panel whose peak is 1e-13 has nearly zero net rates, not a busy chemistry.
A ranking of net rates is not a sensitivity: a large rate may not control the outcome, and a small one may.
A species trace with a vertical step has too few output points near ignition to resolve it.
A mismatch between the title (mole fraction) and the axis (Y) can mislead a reader by a factor of the molar-mass ratio.
must_check: At which moment in the run the ROPs are evaluated (initial state, ignition, or averaged): not stated.
Each panel states its normaliser (done: peak |ROP|, in the title).
The same reaction order or a stated sort rule: panels are sorted by size, so reaction order differs panel to panel.
Species traces state mole or mass fraction consistently.
Ignition time is marked on the species trace.
as_drawn: Peak |ROP| ranges over about 18.6 decades across the nine panels (7.18e5 / 1.84e-13, computed).
Species trace: the printed mole fractions give phi = (0.4615 / 0.03846) / 2 = 6.0 (computed), consistent with the title.
The plotted y values at t = 0 (H2 about 0.0575, O2 about 0.076) match mass fractions computed from the title's mole fractions (0.0575 and 0.0761), not mole fractions.
Ignition at about 1.64 ms (read by eye); final H2O about 0.0857 is the value computed from complete conversion of O2 to water by 2 H2 + O2 -> 2 H2O.

terms.meaning: The net speed of one elementary reaction: forward rate minus reverse rate, in mol per cubic metre per second.

terms.term: Net rate of production of a species
terms.meaning: The sum of the rates of progress of all reactions weighted by the species' stoichiometric coefficients.
Each bar divided by the panel's largest absolute value, so every panel runs from -1 to +1 and relative ranking is visible.
A reaction that makes more radicals than it consumes, such as H + O2 giving O + OH. It drives the exponential growth before ignition.
Species share of mass or of moles. They differ by the ratio of the species' molar mass to the mixture's.
The set of reactive species (H, O, OH, HO2, H2O2) that carry the chain. Its growth sets the ignition delay.
The time before ignition during which the radical pool grows and temperature changes little.

remember: Net ROP = forward minus reverse; blue bars are positive, red are negative.
Normalising each panel hides absolute magnitude: always read the panel title.
Ignition has an induction period (slow) and a thermal runaway (fast).
Mass fraction Y and mole fraction X differ: check which one the axis shows.
A species balance can be checked by hand: complete conversion in 2 H2 + O2 -> 2 H2O fixes the final water.

understand.title: Reading a spectrum
understand.text: Each panel is a ranked list. The longest bar is the fastest net reaction at that condition; the sign shows direction. At 1000 K and 100 atm the leader moves hydrogen to water through OH; at higher temperature the radical-making steps lead. The leader is the reaction to check first when a model disagrees with data at that condition.

understand.title: Why the 2800 K and 0.1 atm panels look odd
understand.text: At 2800 K and 0.1 atm the printed peaks are about 1e-11 and 1e-13 mol/(m^3 s), so almost nothing is happening net. A plausible reading, which the figure does not state, is that the state is close to equilibrium so that forward and reverse rates nearly cancel, and the sign of the leader is then a small difference. Normalisation makes the panel look as informative as the others; the title says it is not.

understand.title: The shape of an ignition
understand.text: On the trace the H2O2 line grows smoothly for 1.6 ms while the major species barely move. Then, within a few microseconds, the fuel and oxidiser are consumed, water appears and the radicals disappear. The step is so fast on the 2 ms axis that it looks vertical.

steps.title: Rate of progress of one reaction
steps.note: Forward minus reverse. Concentrations c in mol per cubic metre. The sign of q is the colour of the bar.

steps.title: From reactions to species
steps.note: Each reaction contributes to every species it touches, weighted by the net stoichiometric coefficient.

steps.title: Normalisation per panel
steps.note: The x axis of every panel. The normaliser is printed in the panel title as the peak |ROP|.

steps.title: Orders of magnitude between panels
steps.note: Computed from two panel titles. A normalised bar of height 1 therefore stands for rates that differ by 18 to 19 decades between these two panels.

steps.title: Mass fraction from mole fraction
steps.note: With X = (0.4615, 0.03846, 0.5) for (H2, O2, N2) and molar masses (2.016, 31.998, 28.014), the mean molar mass is 16.17 and Y(H2) = 0.0575, Y(O2) = 0.0761: the values on the trace at t = 0.

steps.title: Final composition by stoichiometry
steps.note: At phi = 6 oxygen is the limiting reagent, so all of it ends up as water. This reproduces the plateau on the trace, which is a check that the run conserves mass.

steps.title: Equivalence ratio from the printed fractions
steps.note: The stoichiometric hydrogen-to-oxygen ratio is 2, so the title's mixture is phi = 6, as printed.

worked.title: Check the species trace against the title
worked.problem: The title gives mole fractions H2 : O2 : N2 = 0.461538 : 0.0384615 : 0.5. Compute the initial mass fraction of H2 and compare it with the trace.
worked.answer: 0.0575, which is exactly the starting value of the blue line. So the y axis is a mass fraction, while the title says mole fraction.

analyze.q: Why is the leading reaction in the 2800 K, 0.1 atm, phi 0.3 panel reverse (red) while at 1000 K, 100 atm the leaders are forward (blue)?
analyze.hint: Think of which direction the net flow goes when the system is near equilibrium.

analyze.q: At what stage of the run do you think the ROPs were evaluated? Which clue on the figure would settle it?
analyze.hint: The figure does not say; state your assumptions.

analyze.q: H2O2 rises steadily and then vanishes at ignition. What does that say about its role?
analyze.hint: It stores radicals during the induction period and releases them at runaway.

evaluate.q: Is per-panel normalisation the right choice here? Propose an alternative that keeps both ranking and magnitude.
evaluate.hint: Add the absolute peak as a bar or use a common log axis.

evaluate.q: The page calls this a spectrum of production. Judge the title against what the figure shows.
evaluate.hint: It plots net rate of progress per reaction, not per-species production.

create: Redraw the species trace on a log time axis around ignition with the ignition time marked and the title corrected to mass fraction.
Design a panel that shows the three leading reactions' normalised rate against time through ignition.

checks.q: What does a red bar mean?
checks.answer: The net rate of progress is negative: the reverse direction of the written reaction is faster than the forward one.

checks.q: Mixture of H2 and O2 with X(H2)/X(O2) = 4 (no diluent). What is phi?
Two panels both show a top bar of 1. Can you conclude their reactions run equally fast?
checks.answer: No. Each panel is scaled to its own maximum; the absolute peak printed in the title can differ by many orders of magnitude.

checks.q: The title says mole fraction and the axis says Y with values 0.0575 and 0.076 at t = 0. Which is it?
checks.answer: Mass fraction: the plotted values match Y computed from the title's mole fractions (0.0575, 0.0761), not the mole fractions themselves.

checks.q: How would you mark ignition time on the trace?
checks.answer: Pick a criterion, for example the time of maximum rate of temperature rise or of maximum OH, and draw a vertical line there; state the criterion in the caption.
